The test image shows a tomato stem with an elongated, dark brown/necrotic sunken canker running along the internode, with cracking of the stem tissue. No leaf lesions visible — this is a stem disease. Top candidates: Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers, Bacterial_Canker_And_Wilt_Of_Tomato, Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot.

Now I'll view one reference per candidate class.
I've covered 3 classes so far. Last view — checking Phytophthora_Blight for stem lesion comparison.

**Summary of observations:**

- **Test image**: Brown, elongated, cracked/split stem canker running along a tomato internode. The tissue has opened showing brown necrotic interior with lighter tan margins. Stem otherwise green.

- **Alternaria** (Bugwood_4): Crown-level dark canker; Bugwood_13 & 14 were microscopic views. Visual mismatch — location and darkness differ.

- **Bacterial_Canker** (Bugwood_1, 4, 17): References all showed leaf symptoms (yellowing, marginal necrosis, wilting). But the disease is well-documented to cause exactly this — open, linear, brown longitudinal cracks on stems from *Clavibacter michiganensis*.

- **Sclerotinia** (Bugwood_12): Whole-plant collapse with broader stem rot. No match.

- **Phytophthora_Blight** (Bugwood_21): Complete black stem necrosis/collapse. No match.

The test image's key features — brown (not black), open/cracked, elongated linear canker on an internode — are hallmarks of Bacterial Canker stem symptoms. No white mycelium (rules out Sclerotinia), no black sporulation (rules out Alternaria), no complete blackening (rules out Phytophthora).
